The same 38 purchasing requests went to 5 models from 3 providers, each in a new account. Not one of the 140 orders broke a rule, whichever model placed it. But Gemma 4 31B (open weights) met the kitchen's need in 31 of 38 runs, against 38 of 38 for Claude Opus 5.5. The rules stop a model doing harm. They do not make it a good buyer.

The first full run caught a bug in the gateway's own allergen rule. A buyer's mandate excluded tree nuts. A 3 kg tub of hazelnut spread lists hazelnut as an ingredient and 'tree nuts' only as a possible trace. The rule compared allergen codes one to one, so it took the tub for a trace case and asked a person, and the approver script said yes. Result: 4 orders, one per model, placed after a person approved something no approval should allow.

Fixed in code: excluding a group (tree nuts, cereals with gluten) now also excludes its members (hazelnut, wheat), so the gateway refuses that order outright. The numbers at the top are from the run after the fix.
